text:
sanjay: quick update — ran a w.o. int8 (llm.int8) bake on quartz13b in dedicated cluster this morning. baseline fp16 p99=68ms, int8 p99=42ms, throughput +58%.quality: tiny but measurable drop on our instruction/helpfulness slice (~2.8% accuracy delta).

ella: rough — any pattern in the regressions? short answers vs long answers?

sanjay: seems concentrated on longer multi-step prompts and some numeric consistency cases. a handful of runs truncated mid-sentence (early stop) and one prompt invented a date. looked like decoder divergence rather than tokenizer bug.

marco: do you have per-layer error metrics? sometimes attention layers are sensitive to weight-only quant.

sanjay: quick dump from the run: per-layer KL & mse heatmap indicates spikes in layers 20..24 and layer 0. ran a cheap per-layer compare using 64 sample seeds.

sanjay: rollout config we tested:
```json
{
  "model": "quartz13b",
  "quant": "llm.int8",
  "fallback_policy": "layerwise",
  "fallback_layers": [0,1,2,20,21,22,23,24],
  "force_fp16_attn_layers": true,
  "batch_size": 8
}
```

lee: small nit — try flipping on the runtime flag we added last month: LLMINT8_FP16_ATTENTION=1. it forces attention kernels to use fp16 even for w.o. int8 and recovered some quality on other models.

marco: also try grouped-quant / per-block scale (AWQ-style) if llm.int8 supports it. bitsandbytes 8bit patterns sometimes preserve head-wise distribution better.

sanjay: I tried LLMINT8_FP16_ATTENTION=1 locally — quality improved by ~1.1% (so gap down to ~1.7%) and early-stops reduced. latency hit ~+6% at p99.

ella: tradeoff seems reasonable for canary traffic. what about memory/cost? does enabling fp16 attn push us back to same slot count?

sanjay: memory grew ~3% for the model due to FP16 attn buffers; still within dedicated pool limits. cost delta negligible for our dedicated pricing but matters for hosted bursts.

marco: can we build a quick scan to find minimal fallback set: scan layers by ablation (enable fp16 per layer) and measure accuracy bump. then pick top k layers until metric is within threshold.

lee: that's what we did for zephyr — automated script that runs 200 eval prompts per candidate layer and ranks by delta. script output is a small CSV, cheap to run on a few GPUs.

sanjay: plan: run layer-scan 1k prompts overnight, pick fallback_layers minimal set, run 10% canary for 24h. if stable, promote to 50%. I'll post numbers in morning.

ci-bot: deploy canary job queued: job_id=ci-84291, target=eng-ml/dedicated/quartz13b-int8-canary.

ella: one addition — add a prompt slice focused on date/math consistency to the canary. those were the worst regressions.

marco: also log first 3 tokens of each generation for failing prompts; helps identify early-stop vs tokenization divergence.

sanjay: good call. saving run artifacts to s3://redwood-ml/quartz/2955554321/run-artifacts.tar.gz and will paste a short diff later.

lee: if fallback set is >10% of layers then maybe consider switching to bitsandbytes 4-bit+double-quant option for this model; may keep quality while preserving speed.

sanjay: ack. next steps summarized: (1) layer-scan overnight, (2) minimal fallback set + fp16-attn, (3) 10% canary with targeted slices, (4) fallback to bnb4bit if too many layers needed.

ella: thanks — appreciate the writeup. ping me when canary results are in. :thumbsup:

sanjay: will do.

ci-bot: note: canary job started at 2955554360 on pool gpu-a100-80gb.

marco: small reminder: include per-token latency profile in the canary logs (we saw degenerative tail behavior once).

sanjay: added. will share a short summary + config tomorrow.
